title: Schubert Puzzles and Integrability III: Separated Descents
abstractText: In paper I of this series we gave positive formulae for expanding the product $\mathfrak S^\pi \mathfrak S^\rho$ of two Schubert polynomials, in the case that both $\pi,\rho$ had shared descent set of size $\leq 3$. Here we introduce and give positive formulae for two new classes of Schubert product problems: separated descent in which $\pi$'s first descent occurs at (or after) $\rho$'s last, and almost separated descent in which $\pi$'s first two descents occur at (or after) $\rho$'s last two respectively. In both cases our puzzle formulae extend to $K$-theory (multiplying Grothendieck polynomials), and in the separated descent case, to equivariant $K$-theory. The two formulae arise (via quantum integrability) from fusion of minuscule quantized loop algebra representations in types $A$, $D$ respectively.

title: Independent associations of kinesiophobia and pain catastrophizing with self-reported and performance-based functional outcomes in male athletes with patellofemoral pain syndrome: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Background Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) is associated with persistent pain and functional limitations. Although kinesiophobia and pain catastrophizing have been linked to pain-related disability, their distinct associations with self-reported and performance-based functional outcomes remain unclear. Objective To examine the independent associations of kinesiophobia and pain catastrophizing with self-reported knee function and performance-based functional outcomes in male athletes with PFPS. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 61 male athletes with patellofemoral pain syndrome (aged 18–45 years) completed the Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale, and Kujala Patellofemoral Scale. Performance-based function was assessed using the step-down, bilateral squat, single-leg hop, side-hop, and modified Star Excursion Balance Tests. Pearson correlation analyses were performed, followed by eight separate hierarchical multiple linear regression models, one for each functional outcome. Age, body mass index, pain duration, and pain intensity were entered in the first block, followed by kinesiophobia and pain catastrophizing in the second block. Results Both psychological variables were negatively correlated with self-reported knee function and several performance-based outcomes. After adjustment for age, body mass index, pain duration, pain intensity, and pain catastrophizing, greater kinesiophobia was significantly associated with lower Kujala scores (B = − 0.991, SE = 0.143, 95% CI: −1.278 to − 0.704; β = −0.760; p < 0.001). The final model explained 67.8% of the variance in Kujala scores (adjusted R² = 0.642), with a significant incremental contribution from the psychological variables (ΔR² = 0.455, p < 0.001). Multicollinearity was not severe (TSK VIF = 2.024). Greater pain catastrophizing was associated with fewer step-down repetitions (B = − 0.185, 95% CI: −0.364 to − 0.006; β = −0.341; p = 0.043). Neither psychological variable showed a statistically significant individual adjusted association with bilateral squat, single-leg hop, side-hop, or MSEBT performance. Conclusion Greater kinesiophobia was associated with poorer self-reported knee function in male athletes with PFPS, whereas pain catastrophizing showed a modest association with step-down performance. Although the association between kinesiophobia and self-reported function was relatively large and remained significant after adjustment for demographic and clinical characteristics, its magnitude should be interpreted cautiously because of the modest sample size, potential unmeasured confounding, and overlapping constructs and shared reporting processes between self-reported measures. The association with step-down performance also warrants caution because of multiple comparisons. These findings suggest that psychological assessment may complement physical evaluation; however, causal relationships and treatment implications cannot be established from this cross-sectional study. Replication in larger independent samples is needed to confirm the robustness and clinical relevance of these associations.

title: Efficacy and safety of chemoradiation with cisplatin plus capecitabine in localized squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal
abstractText: Background Localized Squamous Cell Anal Cancer (SCCAC) is a rare disease. The standard of care treatment with curative intent is chemoradiation (CRT) with mitomycin (MMC) or cisplatin (CDDP) plus infusional 5-Fluoracil (5-FU). Capecitabine may replace 5-FU in MMC doublet. However, MMC and infusional pumps are frequently unavailable in underdeveloped countries. CCDP and capecitabine are widely available, but there is no prospective data about the feasibility and efficacy of this combination in a definitive SCCAC CRT setting. Methods A Prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of treatment with chemoradiation with CDDP 60mg/m2 D1 and D29 plus Capecitabine 825mg/m2 BID in a population without MMC and infusional pump access. Eligible patients (pts) had T2-4, N0-3, and M0 disease candidates for a full curative CRT regimen. The study data were prospectively collected using REDCap. The primary endpoint was the response by RECIST v.1.1 at 24 weeks(w). The secondary endpoints included toxicity by CTCAE v.5.0, PFS, and OS. Results We enrolled 40 consecutive pts between Aug/2019-Dec/2022 in a tertiary cancer center in Brazil. The median age was 61.6y, the majority were stage III (n = 31, 77.5%) and ECOG 1 (n = 20, 50%). HIV + serology was observed in 11 pts (27,5%). All patients received CRT, with a median dose of 54Gy in the primary tumor and 45Gy in the elective nodes. At 8w, 35% (n = 14) had a complete response (CR), 50% (n = 20) partial response (PR), and 2.5% (n = 1) progressive disease (PD). Considering the 35 participants evaluable for response at 24 weeks months by RECIST v.1.1, the disease control rate was 88.5% (n = 31). CR was observed in 47,5% (n = 19), PR in 20% (n = 8), and PD in 12,5% (n = 5). 11 pts had disease recurrence, and six died. The 1y estimated OS was 94.7% (IC95%: 80.7–98.6%), and 1y estimated PFS was 75.3% (IC95%:57.8–86.3%). Colostomy-free survival at one year was 89.6% (IC95%: 74.7–95.9%). Regarding toxicities, any grade 3/4 toxicity was present in 45% (n = 18) being the main G3/4 clinical toxicity radiodermatitis. Conclusions The CRT regimen with C + CDDP represents an alternative treatment for localized anal canal tumors in a population that does not have access to MMC and 5-FU infusion pumps. Further studies in this population are encouraged to confirm these findings.

title: On the Thresholds of Degenerate Hypergraphs
abstractText: Fix $d>0,\alpha,\epsilon\in(0,1]$. An $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ is $(d,\alpha,\epsilon)$-degenerate if $m_1(G)\le{d+\frac{d}{\log_2 n}}$ and $e\left(G[U]\right)\le{d\left(|U|-1\right)-\alpha}$ for every subset $U\subseteq{V(G)}$ of size $2\le|U|\le{\epsilon n}$. These hypergraphs encompass several natural (hyper)graph classes, including $d$-degenerate hypergraphs for integers $d\ge2$, planar graphs, and powers of cycles. In this paper, we consider the appearance threshold of a $(d,\alpha,\epsilon)$-degenerate hypergraph with bounded maximum degree in the Erdős–Rényi model. We show that $G^{(k)}(n,p_n)$ contains $G_n$ with high probability whenever $p_n=\omega(n^{-1/d})$, improving previous results of Riordan and Kelly–Müyesser–Pokrovskiy.

title: Characteristics and HIV-related engagement of male sexual partners of female sex workers in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA): a scoping review
abstractText: Introduction Understanding the characteristics and behaviors of male sexual partners of female sex workers (FSWs) is crucial for comprehending the dynamics of HIV transmission. We aimed to explore and quantify the existing literature on male sexual partners of FSWs in SSA, where HIV prevalence is high and the dynamics of sex work are poorly understood. We focused on the proportions of men reporting sex with FSWs, along with their characteristics, HIV prevalence, and engagement with HIV services among the general population and specific subgroups. Methods We searched the literature in the EBSCOhost databases (Medline Complete, Global Health, and CINAHL). We included quantitative epidemiological peer-reviewed articles published in English between January 2010 and December 2023, following PRISMA guidelines for scoping reviews. The last search was performed on 09 October 2024. Eligible studies focused on men from the general population and subgroups of men who reported having sex with FSWs. The results were synthesized narratively to identify patterns and gaps in the literature. Results We identified 2,067 articles and reviewed 15, including one meta-analysis. The general population meta-analysis and the articles among subgroups revealed variations in reporting sex with FSWs, differences in HIV prevalence, suboptimal HIV testing uptake, and inconsistent condom use. The proportion of general population men in SSA who had ever paid for sex was 8.5%, with a pooled HIV prevalence of 3.6% and 67.5% reported condom use at last paid sex. High-risk subgroups of men reported different rates of sex with FSWs, ranging from 6.6% to 74%. HIV prevalence also varied significantly, from 7.5% to 26%. Across these high-risk groups, suboptimal HIV testing uptake and inconsistent condom use were common, with no comparative data for men who did not have sex with FSWs. Discussion Men who have sex with FSWs cannot be identified by specific characteristics. High-risk subgroups reported greater engagement with FSWs. Sex with an FSW was associated with higher HIV prevalence among men in the general population, with no data on subgroups. These findings highlight the need for tailored, occupation-specific interventions that address the unique needs of mobile and high-risk men.

title: Allosteric Control and Glycan Shielding Adaptations in the SARS-CoV-2 Spike from Early to Peak Virulence
abstractText: The SARS-CoV-2 Spike glycoprotein is central to viral infectivity and immune evasion, making it a key target for vaccine and therapeutic design. This trimeric peplomer undergoes dynamic conformational changes, particularly in its Receptor Binding Domain (RBD), which transitions between closed (down) and ACE2-accessible (up) states relative to the rest of the protein, to facilitate host cell entry. Structural understanding of such critical interdomain motions, as well as epitope exposure quantification, is essential for obtaining an effective biochemical handle over this protein and, in turn, exploiting it toward improved immunogen development. Focusing on the early circulating D614G form and the later emerging Delta (B.1.617.2) variant with higher virulence, we performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of the soluble form of the Spike in both “down” and “up” conformations of the RBD. Guided by differences in domain-scale fluctuations, we constructed targeted reaction coordinates capturing NTD and RBD rotations and tilting motions, enabling variant-specific structural distinctions to be quantitatively extracted. Conformational landscape mapping and principal component analysis (PCA) reveal a previously uncharacterized dynamic coupling between the NTD and RBD, wherein tilting motions of the NTD are coupled to RBD gating on the neighboring protomer. While several elements of this interdomain coupling are conserved, the Delta variant exhibits a more constrained and functionally optimized RBD-up conformation that favors ACE2 engagement. Concurrently, Delta-specific mutations restructure NTD-local glycans to enhance shielding of the immunogenic supersite, diminishing neutralizing antibody accessibility. Finally, the D950N substitution at the heptad repeat HR1 helix reshapes long-range interactions and alters bending/twisting dynamics of the Spike stalk, likely contributing to both fusion efficiency and immune evasion. Together, these simulations uncover chemically encoded strategies of variant adaptation─through long-range allostery, glycan repositioning, and conformational bias─that shape Spike structure and function. These biochemical and structural insights offer valuable guidance for rational vaccine and therapeutic design against SARS-CoV-2 and emerging variants.

title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films
abstractText: Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that precise control of nominal precursor loading and oxygen partial pressure during direct liquid injection chemical vapor deposition enables a transition in epitaxial Bi4Ti3O12 thin films from two-dimensional growth to dislocation-mediated, chiral spiral growth. This work introduces growth spirals as a controllable route to engineer defect topology and grain morphology, rather than relying on post-growth or stochastic defect formation. Atomic-resolution microscopy and piezoresponse force microscopy reveal that chiral spiral-mediated morphologies exhibit a 135% higher local vertical piezoresponse amplitude and a reduced local vertical switching bias from ±20 to ±5 V compared with two-dimensional films. High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) displacement mapping and density functional theory indicate that out-of-phase boundary defect-associated local structural distortions modify local symmetry, bonding, and strain in a manner consistent with an enhanced out-of-plane polarization component and local vertical electromechanical response. These results establish spiral-driven defect topology as a growth-controlled pathway for tuning the local vertical piezoresponse in layered ferroelectrics and suggest a broadly applicable design principle for future low-power vertical ferroelectric oxide devices.

title: Functionalized bilayer scaffold-mediated spatiotemporal regulation of regenerative immune microenvironment, endogenous stem-cell recruitment, and differentiation for osteochondral regeneration
abstractText: Functional regeneration of osteochondral defects is still hindered by poor spatiotemporal coordination, insufficient endogenous stem-cell recruitment, oxidative stress, and unresolved inflammatory microenvironments that drive apoptosis. To address these challenges, we designed a magnesium diboride (MgB 2 )-functionalized bilayer scaffold for spatiotemporally coordinated endogenous osteochondral regeneration. The upper gelatin-dopamine/hyaluronic acid methacrylate (GelDA/HAMA) layer mimics cartilage extracellular matrix and forms a chondroinductive niche. The bilayer scaffold promotes the recruitment and subsequent retention of endogenous stem/progenitor cells, with synovial fluid-derived mesenchymal stem cells (SF-MSCs) as a representative in vitro model, enabled by catechol-mediated adhesion and integrin–arginine–glycine–aspartic acid (RGD) interactions. The lower three-dimensional (3D)-printed MgB 2 @poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) (PLGA) scaffold mimics bone stiffness and releases Mg 2+ and H 2 in a time-dependent manner, scavenging excess reactive oxygen species during the early inflammatory phase and polarizing macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Sustained Mg 2+ release subsequently supports SF-MSC chondrogenesis and bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) osteogenic mineralization. In a rabbit full-thickness osteochondral defect model, hematoxylin and eosin staining and Safranin-O/Fast Green staining suggested cartilage-like and bone-like tissue formation, while lineage-specific maturation was further supported by immunostaining, including type II collagen (COL II) for cartilage and type I collagen (COL I) for bone, particularly in the MBPH group. This study presents a cell-free and growth-factor-free strategy that leverages the multifunctional bioactivity properties of MgB 2 to coordinate immunomodulation, redox homeostasis, and dual-lineage differentiation for osteochondral repair.

title: The use of Mendelian randomization to explore the causal consequences of childhood maltreatment: consideration of assumptions and challenges
abstractText: Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to strengthen causal inference and has been applied to study the effects of childhood maltreatment on mental health outcomes. However, interpreting MR findings for complex social exposures is challenging due to the complex causal pathways, how they are reported, and potential violations of MR assumptions. Here, we assess the feasibility of applying MR to complex social traits using the association between childhood maltreatment and mental health and behavioral outcomes as an example. We explore four key concerns: confounding by population phenomena, pleiotropy, reverse causality, and selection. For each concern, we demonstrate scenarios where MR studies of childhood maltreatment may be biased using DAGs and critical appraisal of previous MR analyses. For confounding by population phenomena, we further perform within-family genetic analyses in 42,101 parent-offspring trios from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) to address bias due to confounding by parental genotype since childhood maltreatment often occurs within households. Adjusting for parental polygenic risk scores for childhood maltreatment (PRS CM ) resulted in modest same-trait attenuation (11%) for the association between children’s PRS CM and mothers’ report of children’s physical abuse, but cross-trait associations with children’s mental health and behavioral outcomes remained unchanged. The lack of cross-trait shrinkage suggests that genetic variants associated with childhood maltreatment may capture broader child- and family-level phenotypes rather than the exposure itself. Our findings highlight the challenges of interpreting MR studies of childhood maltreatment and suggest caution when using genetic instruments for complex social exposures in psychiatric research.

title: Language usage modulates the neural mechanisms of selective attention in bilinguals
abstractText: The use of multiple languages modulates the neural mechanisms of selective attention, but it is unclear whether these adaptations require continuous engagement and active second language usage. Here we examined whether language usage shapes selective attention in bilingualism, and what neural processes this might engage. 48 highly proficient English-French bilinguals listened to naturalistic speech streams in their first or second language, paired with either linguistic or non-linguistic interference. Participants were matched on their L2 proficiency, but were either Active, Moderate, or Inactive users of their second language. The results revealed usage-related modulation of oscillatory activity in the alpha band, with increased power in Active and Moderate users and decreased alpha power in Inactive bilinguals, and behavioural comprehension accuracy mirroring this pattern of results. In contrast, there was no robust association between usage and perceptual tracking of speech, as captured by mTRF decoding of speech envelopes across frequency bands. Taken together, our findings suggest L2 usage may be modulating the neural mechanisms of auditory selective attention in bilinguals primarily through the top-down attentional allocation, without substantially altering the neural tracking of speech itself.

title: Efficacy of high volume pericapsular nerve group block in patients with acetabular fracture for positioning for subarachnoid block: a pilot study
abstractText: Background: Positioning the patients with acetabular fracture surgeries for neuraxial anesthesia is extremely painful and systemic opioids have limited efficacy. High volume pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block is known to provide a good analgesia for pain around hip but has not been investigated for fracture acetabulum. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the efficacy of high-volume PENG block in improving analgesia and enabling patient positioning for subarachnoid block. Methods: We conducted a prospective single group interventional pilot study in level 1 trauma center in Northern India. Patients between 18 and 75 years of age and ASA physical status of 1 or 2 were enrolled with acetabular fracture scheduled for open reduction and internal fixation (anterior approach) surgery. We assessed numerical rating scale (NRS) score for pain at supine and sitting position and the maximum sitting angle before and 30 minutes after administration of 30ml PENG block. Any need for rescue analgesia and assistance for maintaining the position were noted. Results: A total of 14 patients were recruited. There was a significant decrease in NRS score before and after intervention (supine mean NRS score before vs after block: 3.85±1.4 vs 0.5±0.85, p <0.001; sitting mean NRS score before vs after block: 7.64±1.33 vs 2.21±1.62, p <0.001) along with significant improvement in sitting angle (before vs after block: 35.35 0 ±8.42 0 vs 87.85º±4.25, p <0.001). Conclusions : High-volume PENG block significantly reduces pain scores and increases sitting angle during positioning for neuraxial anesthesia in patients with acetabular fracture. Study was registered on 06/10/2021 in the clinical trial registry of India (www.ctri.nic.in) with unique ID number: CTRI/2021/10/037143.

title: Methodological quality scale: convergent and discriminant validity evidence
Heat current method for analyzing innovatively configured water-enhanced turbofan engine
abstractText: The urgent need for green transformation in aviation, coupled with the demand for integrated and intelligent onboard energy management, imposes stringent requirements on the simulation of novel thermodynamic system configurations. Conventional approaches, which rely on solving coupled governing equations of each component through iterative convergence along the fluid path, require extensive computations to resolve nonlinear implicit constraints, resulting in low efficiency. These limitations are exacerbated by growing system complexity and component diversity, making such methods increasingly unsuitable for modern development requirements. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an isomorphic modeling approach and a hierarchical, categorized solving strategy, both founded on the universal principles of differentiated transport characteristics, to establish a heat-current-based framework for analyzing complex thermodynamic systems with novel configurations. Applied to a water-enhanced turbofan (WET) engine and validated against MTU's published data and the GasTurb benchmark, the heat current method achieves a maximum deviation of only 1.81%, significantly outperforming MTU's reported deviation of 6.60%. Furthermore, using this method, we elucidate the thermodynamic parameter-matching relationships within the WET engine and propose an improved system design incorporating ammonia-fuel enhanced recuperation. These results demonstrate the method’s strong potential for quantitative analysis and optimization of advanced thermodynamic systems in innovative configurations.

title: The Rank-Nullity Ring of a Matroid
abstractText: We introduce the rank-nullity ring of a matroid $M$, which is a subring of the Chow ring of the permutahedral toric variety. This subring contains the tautological Chern classes of $M$, a fact we deduce from a highly symmetric formula for these classes. When the matroid $M$ is a uniform matroid, the rank-nullity ring coincides with the subring of $S_n$-invariants of the Chow ring of the permutahedral toric variety. In this case, we compute its Hilbert function explicitly and provide a Gröbner basis for the ideal of relations among its generators.

title: Physiologically realistic gamma activity produced in silico by weakening the PING attractor state
abstractText: Network oscillations in the gamma (30-80 Hz) frequency range are implicated in many vital neurological functions. The seminal Pyramidal Interneuron Network Gamma (PING) mechanism produces gamma oscillations in silico with dynamics associated with a strongly attracting limit cycle. However, this activity is stronger and more stable than what is observed during in vivo gamma oscillations, which are transient and driven by sparse spiking activity. Here we describe multiple biophysically motivated changes degenerately driving PING-motivated networks to produce more realistic gamma activity. Increased heterogeneity, synapse-like noise, and a depolarized chloride reversal potential each destabilize the attractor represented by PING-driven activity: minor alterations disrupt the unrealistic organization of idealized PING oscillations, while larger changes entirely prevent this overly-synchronous network activity. This allows new dynamics to emerge: spontaneous and transient increases in gamma-band oscillatory power with excitatory cells only weakly entrained to the population rhythm. These features, better approximating the in vivo reality, mirror a system’s oscillatory return to a stable focus following noise-induced perturbations. In fact, dynamical systems with both a stable focus and limit cycle are associated with Hopf bifurcations, which have been characterized in models of reciprocally connected excitatory and inhibitory neuronal populations as required for PING. We therefore propose a revised explanation for physiologically-realistic gamma activity that retains the key elements of the PING mechanism—strong reciprocal connection between excitatory and inhibitory neurons—but where biophysical phenomena bias the system towards damped oscillations around a weakly stable focus rather than a stable limit cycle. Significance Statement The mechanisms underlying network oscillations at gamma frequencies have long been a focus of computational neuroscience. This research has produced idealized mechanisms yielding highly synchronous, active, and stable oscillations; however, in vivo gamma rhythms are transient with sparse neuronal spiking. Here, we illustrate minimal, biophysically relevant adjustments to established Pyramidal Interneuron Network Gamma (PING) networks that bridge a major divide between these traditional in silico systems and the experimental reality. Uncorrelated noisy input and a depolarized chloride reversal potential disrupt stereotyped PING rhythms and promote more realistic transient increased gamma power in network activity. This important step forward in the modeling of gamma oscillations illustrates how including biophysical detail can promote more realistic activity in computational systems.

What Fraction of the Vertex Set of a Graph can be Covered by $k$ Neighborhoods?
abstractText: Let $k\ge 2$ be a fixed integer, $0<c<1$ a constant. Consider a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and average degree $cn$. We answer a question of Simon Griffiths by showing that $G$ has $k$ vertices such that their neighborhoods together cover at least $\min\bigl(1-(1-c)^{k},\sqrt{c}\,\bigr)n$ vertices. This result is essentially tight.

title: Carrion crows are sensitive to human head, but not eye, orientation
abstractText: Escape is a vital survival mechanism, shaped by numerous factors relating to risk assessment. Birds rely on flight as a primary escape mechanism with flight initiation distance (FID) commonly used to quantify responses. In this study we tested whether carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) were sensitive to human gaze when approached with direct gaze and head orientation, direct head but averted eyes, or averted head and eyes. We also explored how contextual variables such as the birds’ initial direction, starting distance, temperature, and weather affect FID. We observed 172 naturally foraging crows randomly assigned to one of three gaze conditions. Each was approached by the experimenter, while recording their position throughout. Once the subject left their initial location, the distance between experimenter’s initial position and subject’s location (starting distance), where the experimenter stopped and the subject’s location (FID), and environmental and situational factors were recorded. Results demonstrated a significant difference in FID based on gaze condition: FID was about 3.5 m shorter when head and eyes were averted than when both were direct or head was direct and eyes were averted. Initial direction and starting distance also significantly affected FID but weather and temperature had no significant effects. These findings suggest that carrion crows are sensitive to human head orientation but not eye direction specifically. They also contribute to our understanding of human-wildlife interactions.

title: Bridging the Digital Divide: How ICT Expansion Shapes Secondary Enrollment and Gender Equity in Education
abstractText: This study investigates the role of information and communication technologies (ICTs) in shaping secondary school enrollment and gender equity across 72 developing countries from 2000 to 2023. Using fixed-effects panel models with controls for income, urbanization, and fertility, the analysis tests two hypotheses: (H1) ICT expansion increases secondary enrollment; and (H2) ICT expansion enhances gender parity in secondary education. The findings confirm H1, showing that ICT expansion significantly improves enrollment rates, though the effect weakens once global time trends are controlled. The evidence for H2 is more nuanced: while the positive association with gender parity remains strong in baseline specifications , a sub group analysis by income level reveals that this equity-enhancing effect is statistically significant only for Low-Income Countries, becoming insignificant for Middle-Income Countries. Robustness checks also reveal that digitalization’s impact on enrollment was strongest during the early adoption phase (pre-2010). The results highlight ICT's dual dividend: (1) expanding educational access and (2) reducing gender gaps yet also underscore the need for complementary policies addressing fertility, affordability, and rural digital infrastructure. The study contributes to debates on ICT for development by offering long-term, within-country evidence on the educational dividends of digitalization.

title: Nanostructure of PEGDA-PEG Hydrogel Membranes and How It Controls Their Permeability
abstractText: The spatial heterogeneity of hydrogels composed of PEGDA and added polymer chains is expected to play a crucial role in their transport properties, which can be exploited in filtration or tissue engineering. However, little is known about the arrangement of the polymer chains in the matrix and the length scales of these heterogeneities. Here, we combine solid-state NMR and small angle neutron scattering to unravel the structure and dynamics of PEGDA hydrogels containing added PEG chains of various concentrations. Using NMR, we find that the PEG segments of the PEGDA matrix present more constrained dynamics when PEG chains are added, which is probably due to entanglements between the PEG chains and the PEGDA matrix consistent with previous results in our group, which showed that the added PEG chains are trapped within the PEGDA/PEG hydrogels. Using SANS, contrast matching enables us to obtain specifically the SANS signal of the PEG-d chains in the PEGDA matrix. The scattering curves, fitted with a Lorentzian model, yield a correlation length much larger than the ones obtained for the solutions containing only PEG. At the scale of tens of nanometers, the samples present heterogeneities in both the PEGDA and PEG concentrations. When plotting the water permeability of the hydrogel membranes, K, as a function of the specific surface of the PEGDA heterogeneities, we obtain a master curve, showing that the heterogeneity of the PEGDA matrix controls the permeability of the sample. Moreover, the scaling K ∝ V/S suggests a structure composed of facetted PEGDA/PEG heterogeneities separated by a network of aqueous thin and flattened films in which the water can permeate.

title: Optimization Problem for Star Covers of Graphs without Four Cycles
abstractText: The symmetric nonnegative trifactorization of matrices motivates the study of the SNT-rank of graphs. We focus on the family of graphs characterized by three forbidden closed $4$-walks and show that the calculation of the SNT-rank of graphs from this family can be formulated as an optimization problem for star covers on graphs. Unlike traditional optimization that minimizes the number of stars, our objective is to minimize the number of components used in the cover, where each star is a join of two components. We introduce a graph parameter $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ and show that for a graph $G$ from the family in question it is equal to the difference between the number of vertices in the graph and the minimal number of components needed in any star cover of $G$. We develop an algorithm for computing $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ consisting of three main steps: (1) transformation of $G$ to a weighted multigraph $\Gamma$, (2) reduction of $\Gamma$ to a multigraph $\tau(\Gamma)$ with all edge weights equal to $0$ and all vertex degrees at least three, (3) iterative process for computing $\operatorname{gap}(G)$ by removing vertices in $\tau(\Gamma)$. While steps (1) and (2) are straightforward and control the $\operatorname{gap}$, step (3) is computationally complex but allows us to compute the $\operatorname{gap}$ for any graph in the considered family.

title: The System for Assessing the Effects of Investment Projects in the Knowledge Base of IEIE SB RAS
abstractText: The article examines the development of approaches to data analysis and structuring using the example of the development of the Knowledge Base of the The Institute of Economics and Industrial Engineering within the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IEIE SB RAS). The main purpose of creating a knowledge base is to transform the source data on resources, facilities, technologies, the state and development of the Asian Russia macro-region, which will provide a qualitatively new understanding of complex processes of synergy in the economy based on network combinations of chains of objects interconnected by the movement of natural, financial, labor, information resources, products, technologies, supported by development institutions. Special attention is paid to the task of assessing the effects of the implementation of investment projects. To solve it, the knowledge base accumulates data on investment projects, companies, socio-economic indicators and technologies. The text describes concepts and approaches to creating a consistent model package, including a model and analytical apparatus for evaluating effects at the macro, meso, and micro levels. The described model complex includes a block of intersectoral models, network and cognitive models, forecasting models for socio-economic statistics, assessment systems for commercial and indirect effects, as well as a block of models based on microeconomic data linked to Gis space. A comprehensive model analysis of investment projects, taking into account spatial effects, will make it possible to more accurately and comprehensively assess the socio-economic consequences for the economy and offset the limitations and measurement errors of individual methods.

title: Development of SELF and IDEAL body size perception in children aged 6–12 years
abstractText: Background: Several studies have investigated children’s body image using figure rating scales, and found females’ selection of IDEAL (ideal body image) was significantly thinner than SELF (perceived current body image) and males’ selection of IDEAL. However, no studies have investigated children’s body image using virtual reality avatars. This study examined whether the discrepancy between SELF and IDEAL is greater in female than in male children aged 6 to 12 years using photorealistic figure rating scales. Methods: Female and male photorealistic body size scales based on Body Mass Index (BMI) were created using MakeHuman and Blender, and children rated their SELF and IDEAL body images using these scales. Results: Discrepancy between SELF and IDEAL body image was present among younger female (6.3–8.5 years) and older (10.3–12.5 years) elementary school children, but not among middle elementary school children (8.3–10.5 years). Conclusion: These findings suggest that body dissatisfaction, similar to that observed in adult females, emerges or is already formed at an early age. Trial registration: Not applicable.

title: Integrating water temperature, conductivity, and streamflow to assess the impact of watershed dynamics on chattahoochee river in the United States
abstractText: Rivers are essential for sustaining human activities, ecological balance, and water supply. However, urbanization remains a major factor ​controlling quality of rivers. Several studies have been conducted to examine hydrological processes and watersheds impacts on river water quality; yet fewer studies have only utilized high-frequency monitoring data or considered few parameters like temperature and conductivity alone to capture the effects of urbanization on water quality dynamics in natural and engineered river systems. This study integrates high-resolution (15-minute interval) measurements of streamflow, precipitation, water temperature, and conductance data that were collected over a five-year period (January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025) from multiple monitoring stations along the Chattahoochee River to evaluate the combined effects of hydrology and urbanization on water quality dynamics. Monitoring stations were categorized based on surrounding land cover into a five-class urbanization gradient, ranging from not developed to developed high intensity watersheds. Flow variables such as monthly flow, drainage-adjusted daily flow, and flow flashiness. Trends and relationships between temperature and conductance were examined, ANCOVA and linear mixed models (LMM) were used to examine the relationship between watersheds, hydrologic, and water quality variables. Seasonal flows were generally highest in late winter to early spring months, and differed significantly at ( P < 0.001, α = 0.05). Flow flashiness increased at stations proximal to dams, while urbanized watersheds exhibited moderate to low flashiness. Precipitation showed positive weak relationship with flow but was significant. The results of the ANCOVA revealed that temperature and watersheds influence conductance, while LMM showed that drainage area largely control conductance, while temperature, flow, and watershed subordinately influence conductance. These findings emphasize the importance of integrating high-frequency data with land use components for improved understanding and management of urbanizing river systems.

title: Bayesian optimisation and graph-based rheology enable sequence-dependent modelling of DNA materials
abstractText: Bridging molecular and emergent properties is essential for designing soft matter. Synthetic DNA materials exhibit diverse material properties, but multiscale complexity and a vast sequence design space limit targeted design. We address this challenge with a computational workflow that links sequence-level design to rheological material properties. Concretely, we use machine learning to parametrise scalable, DNA-sequence-aware simulations, which we evaluate using graph-based rheology. We demonstrate this workflow on materials composed of self-interacting, multivalent DNA nanostars assembled from single strands. Structure and flexibility of nanostars are quantified with nucleotide-level oxDNA simulations, enabling Bayesian optimisation of a more coarse-grained bead-spring model. The bead-spring model allows efficient simulation of network formation between nanostars, governed by hybridisation free energies computed with oxDNA and NUPACK. Nanostar valency and network connectivity are translated into rheological material properties with a graph-based method that we extend to include hydrodynamic interactions, yielding good agreement with the experimental reference data. We generalise our findings by analysing theoretical graph representations of DNA materials. As a proof-of-concept, we show how machine learning can optimise sequence affinities to produce desired rheological responses. Our work illustrates how machine learning can bridge scales and automate coarse-graining to facilitate targeted design of DNA materials through sequence-property relationships.

Association of the APOE ε4 allele with spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage in a Chinese Han case–control sample
abstractText: Objective The role of genes, especially APOE, in intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is significant. But ethnic differences on ICH remain unclear, especially in Chinese individuals. We explored the correlation between APOE and ICH in Chinese Han population.. Methods In this single-centre, retrospective, case-control study, we collected clinical data of supratentorial ICH patients and healthy people matched 1:1 with ICH from June 2023 to January 2025. We used the χ 2 test to explore differences in APOE genotypes and allele frequencies between the groups. We established different ICH prediction models with and without APOE data using Machine Learning and compared prediction efficiency by AUC, net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results We enrolled 237 ICH patients and 237 controls. There was a significant difference in ε4 allele distribution between two groups (P = 0.010,OR = 1.813,95% CI (1.149,2.860)); differences remained after stratification by deep ICH (P = 0.015, OR = 1.979, 95% CI (1.135,3.448)). The NRI and IDI between ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8139) and without (AUC = 0.8083) APOE genotypes were 0.3797(P<0.0001) and 0.0106(P = 0.0458). The NRI and IDI between ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8204) and without (AUC = 0.8150) the ε4 allele were 0.3556(P<0.0001) and 0.0090(P = 0.0734). The NRI and IDI between deep ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8182) and without (AUC = 0.8076) APOE genotypes were 0.3949(P = 0.0002) and 0.0202(P = 0.0145). The NRI and IDI between deep ICH prediction models with (AUC = 0.8304) and without (AUC = 0.8223) the ε4 allele were 0.4001(P = 0.0002) and 0.0116(P = 0.0635). Conclusions For Chinese Han population, APOE polymorphisms, especially the ε4 allele, may be risk factors for ICH and deep ICH.

title: First results of sub-arcsecond scale objects identified with ASKAP using interplanetary scintillation
abstractText: We present a catalogue of 131 compact (≲0.1′′) sources detected at 823 MHz via their Interplanetary Scintillation (IPS). These measurements were made with the ASKAP telescope, across its full field of view of 35 square degrees, utilising all 36 phased array feed (PAF) beams. To bypass ASKAP’s standard correlator’s minimum integration limit of 10 s, we used the CRAFT data capture system (CRACO), with visibilities sampled every 110 ms. Here we present the data processing steps, the sources detected, and their IPS-inferred properties. ASKAP IPS cleanly separates two populations: compact hotspots embedded in extended lobes and IPS-unresolved sources which are AGN or CSO sources associated with the galactic nucleus. We also compare these results with the results from observations of IPS at 162 MHz with the Murchison Widefield Array, providing the spectra of compact components between 162 and 888 MHz. These measurements further re-enforce the dominance of peaked-spectrum SEDs in the compact-source population at frequencies below 1 GHz. This pilot study using test data is a pathfinder for a more comprehensive ASKAP IPS survey which is underway.

title: In-vitro Fertilization Outcomes in Females of Advanced Maternal Age with Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome
abstractText: Fertility and assisted reproductive technology (ART) is a fast-growing sub-speciality within Obstetrics and Gynaecology. After the age of thirty-five years, females experience an almost linear decrease in fertility, but in the case of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) there may be an exception to this rule. Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) is a hormone secreted by the granulosa cells which are proliferating in growing follicles and its serum levels as well as antral follicle count on ultrasound are both reliable markers of ovarian reserve. Age-related infertility in women is mainly linked to changes in the ovarian reserve, defined as the quality and number of remaining follicles within the ovaries at a particular age. Both AMH and antral follicle count show a decline with increasing age in normo-ovulatory women, but this kind of age-related decrease is slowed down in patients with PCOS1. PCOS is an endocrine disorder which affects up to 10% of women of reproductive-age and it accounts for up to 25% of infertility among couples1. It is characterized by infrequent ovulation, hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance and a characteristic ultrasonographic ovarian appearance with a high number of antral follicles. This ovarian dysfunction has previously been linked to infertility, but emerging studies suggest that women of advanced maternal age with PCOS display increased follicle and oocyte count during ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval during In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)2. Due to the increased antral follicle count in these patients, one would predict increased oocyte counts, increased number of embryos and higher incidence of pregnancy and live birth rates when compared to age-matched eumenorrheic females3. Some studies suggest that irrespective of increased oocyte yield, fertility outcomes may not vary and that there might be no extension of the reproductive window in PCOS. One must note that if oocyte yield is proven to be increased but live birth rates remain unchanged, there is limited advantage from this variation1. Despite potential increase in pregnancy rates, one must also take into consideration that PCOS is associated with increased rates of miscarriage, pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm delivery and stillbirth4,5.

title: ExFiT: Ensemble-Based Excited-State Character Fingerprinting across Temperatures
abstractText: The character of electronically excited states, such as the balance between local excitation (LE), charge transfer (CT), and the spatial separation of electron and hole densities, strongly influences absorption properties and the electronic-state landscape at the Franck–Condon geometry of organic chromophores, evaluated at ground-state nuclear configurations. Conventional analyses based on single equilibrium geometries neglect thermal fluctuations that can significantly alter this character. We present ExFiT, an ensemble-based computational pipeline that interfaces with GPU-accelerated electronic-structure calculations for fingerprinting excited-state character across temperatures. ExFiT combines finite-temperature Wigner sampling with ensemble-resolved excited-state analysis and principal component analysis to quantify distributions of CT metrics, electron–hole separation, entanglement, and orbital participation. Application to representative chromophores (trans-azobenzene, (E)-hemithioindigo, para-nitroaniline, and coumarin 481) reveals distinct regimes of thermal behavior, ranging from robust excited-state character to broadened descriptor distributions and bright-state reordering associated with closely spaced excited states within the Franck–Condon ensemble. NTO overlap further shows that changes in optical brightness need not reflect changes in excited-state character, distinguishing state perturbation from state reassignment. These results demonstrate how thermal fluctuations modulate excited-state electronic structures and establish the applicability of ExFiT as a framework for generating statistically meaningful initial-condition ensembles for spectral simulations and future nonadiabatic dynamics studies.

title: Fight or faint: Behavioural response and fainting in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) with acute thermal exposure
abstractText: Thermal delousing — the brief immersion of fish in heated water for ~30 seconds — is widely used to control salmon lice infestations in salmonid aquaculture. However, studies of the behavioural responses of fish to the treatment have been limited to Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) and species-specific response of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remains undescribed. This study characterised the behavioural responses of small (~200 g) and large (~2900 g) rainbow trout during sudden exposure for 30 s to water temperatures of 24–34 °C, with focus on the occurrence and duration of loss of equilibrium (LoE) and the influence of acclimation temperature (6 °C and 12 °C) on responses in large trout. Behavioural intensity increased with exposure temperature in both size classes. In small trout, LoE during exposure was rare, though a notable proportion of fish lost equilibrium upon return to ambient temperature. In contrast, most large trout lost equilibrium during exposure, with a higher proportion affected in the 6 °C (94%) than in the 12 °C acclimation group (81%). Duration of LoE was prolonged at 34 °C, with some individuals remaining out of equilibrium for several minutes post-treatment. No mortality was recorded during or within three days following exposure in either trial. The high prevalence and extended duration of LoE in large trout represents a markedly different welfare profile compared to the sustained thrashing behaviour characteristic of Atlantic salmon under equivalent conditions. These findings highlight the importance of species-specific welfare assessments for the development of evidence-based delousing guidelines for rainbow trout.

title: Multi-objective gravity data inversion for basement depth estimation in sedimentary basins
abstractText: Accurate estimation of basement depth is significant in the energy resource exploration and mineral prospecting. Basement depth is inherently controlled by a combination of sedimentation, tectonic subsidence, and geological processes that collectively shape the subsurface architecture. The reconstruction of basement depth and its density variations represents a valuable and well-established application of gravity anomaly inversion. Conventional approaches to generating geologically realistic basement models typically rely on regularization techniques, frequency-domain filtering methods, and smoothness constraints within optimization frameworks to stabilize the inversion process. This study investigates the application of the adaptive multi-objective optimization algorithm (AMALGAM) for accurate characterization of sedimentary basin geometry. Within this optimization framework, gravity data inversion is formulated to simultaneously minimize two competing objective functions, namely, the data misfit term and the model smoothness constraint, thereby eliminating the need for post-inversion smoothing or spectral filtering of model parameters. The multi-objective optimization ensures that one objective does not over-dominate without applying weighting and regularization schemes. The result is an ensemble of non-dominated optimal solutions called the Pareto-optimal set. The robustness and reliability of the proposed algorithm are systematically evaluated and validated using both noise-free and noise-added synthetic gravity datasets. The algorithm’s effectiveness is further demonstrated through its application to gravity anomaly data acquired over two real sedimentary basins. The results confirm that the proposed approach constitutes a promising, accurate, and computationally efficient method for subsurface imaging in geological and geophysical exploration.

title: Comparative Analysis of Objective Weighting Approaches in Multi-Criteria Decision Making Using WASPAS
abstractText: Selecting the best-performing honorary employee is a multi-criteria decision-making problem because employee performance is influenced by several criteria with different levels of importance. This study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of objective weighting approaches in the Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment (WASPAS) method for evaluating honorary employee performance and examining the stability of the resulting rankings. Eight alternatives, namely HE-A to HE-H, were evaluated using five criteria: Work Performance, Discipline, Cooperative Ability, Initiatives and Problem Solving, and Communication Skills. Twelve objective weighting methods, namely Entropy, G2M, RECA, LOPCOW, CRITIC, MEREC, WENSLO, LOGSTA, LODECI, ITARA, SITDE, and DAM, were independently applied to determine criterion weights. The resulting weights were then integrated into WASPAS to generate alternative rankings under different weighting scenarios. The results show that HE-F consistently achieved the first rank across all objective weighting approaches, while HE-E consistently occupied the eighth position. The ranking comparison further indicates that most methods produce ranking patterns close to the original ranking, although MEREC introduces greater changes in several alternative positions. Spearman rank correlation analysis confirms a strong consistency of the resulting rankings, with the highest correlation obtained by LODECI, SITDE, and DAM at 0.9524, followed by G2M and CRITIC at 0.9286 and MEREC at 0.9048. Overall, the findings demonstrate that the combination of objective weighting approaches and WASPAS provides a reliable framework for employee performance evaluation, while comparative correlation analysis can be used to assess ranking stability and robustness across different weighting perspectives.

title: Decision Support System for Production Machine Maintenance Prioritization Using LOPCOW Weighting and SPOTIS
abstractText: Maintenance of production machines is essential for maintaining production continuity and minimizing the risk of downtime and operational losses. However, limited maintenance resources, including budget, technician availability, maintenance time, and spare parts, require organizations to establish appropriate maintenance priorities. This study proposes a Decision Support System (DSS) for objectively prioritizing production machine maintenance using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) approach that integrates the LOPCOW and SPOTIS methods. LOPCOW is applied to determine objective criterion weights based on the characteristics and variation of the maintenance data, while SPOTIS is used to rank production machines according to their distance from the ideal solution. The results show that C7 obtains the highest criterion weight of 0.2616, followed by C5 (0.2134) and C6 (0.1937), while C2 obtains the lowest weight of 0.0412. The SPOTIS results produce the maintenance priority sequence M4, M7, M2, M5, M1, M8, M3, and M6, with M4 achieving the highest priority with a final value of 0.0000, while M6 has the lowest priority with 1.0000. These findings demonstrate that the proposed LOPCOW–SPOTIS framework can provide a systematic, objective, and transparent basis for identifying maintenance priorities and supporting more consistent allocation of limited maintenance resources.

title: Combination of Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Dependence and Simple Additive Weighting Methods for Multi-Criteria Barista Selection: A Decision Support Approach
abstractText: Barista selection is an important process in the coffee shop and hospitality industry because baristas are required to possess not only technical skills but also coffee knowledge, communication, work speed, accuracy, and creativity. Evaluating candidates based on a single criterion can result in subjective and less representative decisions. Therefore, this study aims to develop a Decision Support System (DSS) for barista candidate selection by integrating the Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Dependence (CRITID) and Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) methods. CRITID is applied to determine objective criterion weights by considering data variation and inter-criteria relationships, while SAW is used to calculate preference values and rank the candidates. The results show that Work Speed (CB-06) has the highest criterion weight of 0.1311, followed by Technical Skills (CB-02) with 0.1275 and Coffee Knowledge (CB-04) with 0.1253. The SAW ranking identifies A7 as the highest-ranked candidate with a preference value of 0.9682, followed by A3 with 0.9603 and A8 with 0.8994. Sensitivity analysis involving 32 scenarios with criterion weight changes of ±0.05 and ±0.10 indicates that the ranking structure is relatively stable, with A7 and A3 consistently maintaining the first and second positions. These findings demonstrate that the integration of CRITID and SAW can support a more objective, systematic, measurable, and stable decision-making process for barista candidate selection.

title: A Novel MPSI Weighting and Proximity Indexed Value Framework for Multi-Criteria Selection of Marketplace Logistics Partners
abstractText: In facing the increasingly intense competition in the logistics industry, companies are often confronted with challenges in selecting the most appropriate logistics partner due to the many performance criteria that must be considered simultaneously. This study aims to evaluate and determine the best logistics partner using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making approach through the integration of the MPSI method for criteria weighting and PIV for the alternative ranking process. The criteria used include Transit Time, On-Time Delivery, First-Attempt Success, Attempt Rate, and Package Volume, which are analyzed based on the performance data of each alternative. The weighting results indicate that Package Volume and Transit Time are the most dominant factors in the evaluation process. Based on the PIV method calculations, the ranking results were obtained, with NJ Logistics Partner occupying the first rank with a score of 0.46408, followed by TK Logistics Partner in second place with a score of 0.44014, and JT Logistics Partner in third place with a score of 0.39282. Sensitivity tests through various weight change scenarios showed that the ranking structure remained consistent, indicating that the model has a high level of stability and resilience to parameter variations. Overall, the proposed approach is able to produce decisions that are objective, measurable, and reliable as a basis for supporting strategic logistics partner selection.

title: What makes a strong decision letter to an author?
abstractText: A strong decision letter tells authors why a manuscript was accepted, rejected, or returned for revision. Diane B. Three examples show how to communicate judgment with clarity and kindness.

title: PENERAPAN PENDEKATAN PMRI UNTUK MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI BERPRESTASI SISWA DI MTS MIFTAHUL HUDA AJUNG
abstractText: This study was motivated by students’ low achievement motivation in mathematics learning in Class VII A at MTs Miftahul Huda Ajung. It aimed to improve students’ achievement motivation through the implementation Pembelajaran Matematika Realistik Indonesia (PMRI) approach. This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design conducted collaboratively over two cycles. Each cycle consisted of four stages: planning, action, observation, and reflection. The research participants were 34 students. Data were collected through observations, achievement motivation questionnaires, learning achievement tests, field notes, documentation, and interviews. The data were analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative methods. The results indicated an improvement in students’ achievement motivation and mathematics learning outcomes following the implementation of PMRI. The mean achievement motivation questionnaire score increased from 103.5 in Cycle I to 107.9 in Cycle II, with both scores falling into the high category. The percentage of students achieving learning mastery also increased from 68% in Cycle I to 76% in Cycle II. Furthermore, the average implementation of the learning process in Cycle II reached 96%. These findings suggest that PMRI can serve as an alternative instructional approach to improving students’ achievement motivation and mathematics learning outcomes.

title: L(2,1)-LABELING ON SEVERAL FAMILIES OF STAR GRAPHS
abstractText: This research discusses L(2,1) labeling on some families of star graphs, namely planter graphs (R_n), lilly graphs (l_n), and umbrella graphs (U_(m,n)). The L(2,1) labeling is a type of graph labeling that assigns nonnegative integer labels to each vertex of a graph such that two vertices that are one edge apart have labels that differ by at least two, and two vertices that are two edges apart have labels that differ by at least one. This study uses axiomatic descriptive methods and pattern detection in determining the minimum span value of the L(2,1) labeling, denoted as lambda_2,1(G). The results show that lambda_2,1(R_n) = n+3, lambda_2,1(l_n) = 2n+3, and lambda_2,1(U_(m,n)) = m+2. These three graphs were chosen because their L(2,1) labeling is still an open problem and has not been widely studied in previous literature. This research is expected to contribute to the development of graph labeling theory and serve as an initial reference for future researchers. A suggestion for further research is to explore the minimum value of the L(2,1) labeling range in other classes of graphs that have not yet been determined.

title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
abstractText: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Each stage in the framework may be given arbitrary weights by users, which will decide how essential a step is to them and provide a different score for a particular address. A grid search strategy and a threshold after which the address is deemed Sybil were used to find the optimal weights. This article examined a collection of EOAs from the ZK sync rollup. Ultimately, 76% of the examined accounts were classified as Sybils. Compared to the official ZK sync eligibility list, we found 342 addresses that received airdrop tokens but were marked as Sybil by our solution.

title: Metabolic inflammation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 1.3 billion people worldwide and is frequently associated with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and other metabolic disorders. A key feature linking these conditions is metabolic inflammation, or metainflammation, a state of chronic, low-grade inflammation driven by excessive lipid accumulation and adipose tissue dysfunction. Metainflammation promotes hepatic steatosis, inflammation, hepatocyte injury and ballooning, and fibrosis, thereby contributing to the development and progression of MASLD, as well as metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD), which can lead to liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. These pathological processes are mediated through multiple interconnected mechanisms, including insulin resistance, dysregulated lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, fibrogenesis, and alterations in the gut microbiota. This review discusses the mechanisms underlying metainflammation in MASLD and MetALD and summarizes current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting these pathogenic factors in preclinical studies and clinical trials.

title: Artificial intelligence and the rebalanced hemostasis of chronic liver disease: From viscoelastic testing to digital twins
abstractText: Chronic liver disease, particularly cirrhosis, produces a fragile, rebalanced hemostatic state. Patients may develop bleeding or thrombosis. The international normalized ratio and platelet count incompletely reflect concurrent procoagulant and anticoagulant changes and poorly predict procedural bleeding. Viscoelastic testing and thrombin-generation assays assess hemostasis more broadly. Randomized trials support viscoelastic testing-guided reductions in blood product use, but these trials do not establish prediction of later bleeding or thrombosis. Machine-learning models address gastrointestinal bleeding outcomes, variceal hemorrhage, portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and transfusion requirements using clinical records, imaging, or elastography. Most cirrhosis models address one outcome, omit direct hemostatic measurements, and have limited external validation. Within the English-language eligibility criteria and focused queries of a PubMed update on July 29, 2026, no adult model jointly estimating future bleeding and PVT in cirrhosis was identified. This structured narrative minireview evaluates the evidence for both outcomes and specifies research requirements for paired-risk models and a possible digital twin of the coagulation-portal axis. Treatment-specific predictions would require additional causal validation.

title: Movimiento dentario con alineadores transparentes frente a ortodoncia fija: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: comparar los resultados del movimiento dentario ortodóncico obtenidos con alineadores transparentes y con aparatología fija convencional. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas con metaanálisis, ensayos clínicos y estudios de cohorte. Resultados: ambos sistemas corrigieron maloclusiones leves y moderadas, pero la aparatología fija logró mejores contactos oclusales y un mejor control del torque; la precisión de los alineadores rondó la mitad del movimiento planificado y fue menor en la extrusión y la rotación; los aditamentos mejoraron el control. Los alineadores produjeron menos dolor y mejor salud periodontal. Conclusión: los alineadores son una alternativa eficaz en casos seleccionados, mientras que la aparatología fija sigue siendo más predecible en los movimientos complejos.

title: Cambios bucales durante el embarazo: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los cambios bucales que se producen durante el embarazo, sus mecanismos, sus consecuencias gestacionales y su prevención. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas y narrativas, un estudio observacional, un ensayo clínico y consensos. Resultados: el embarazo aumentó la inflamación gingival sin un aumento proporcional de la placa, por efecto de los estrógenos y la progesterona sobre los vasos, la respuesta inmunitaria y la microbiota. Los cambios salivales y la exposición ácida favorecen la caries y la erosión. La enfermedad periodontal se asoció con resultados gestacionales adversos, aunque su tratamiento no demostró prevenirlos con claridad. Conclusión: el control de placa y la educación prenatal son las medidas con mejor respaldo.

title: Efectos del piercing oral en la salud bucal: complicaciones locales inmediatas y tardías
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre las complicaciones locales inmediatas y tardías del piercing oral en la mucosa y los tejidos blandos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025), complementada con estudios previos de referencia; se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios observacionales, estudios microbiológicos, una intervención educativa y reportes de caso. Resultados: las complicaciones inmediatas más descritas fueron el dolor, el edema, el sangrado y la infección local. Entre las tardías destacaron las lesiones traumáticas e hiperplásicas de la mucosa y la colonización bacteriana de la joya, influida por su material. Se documentaron casos de endocarditis infecciosa. Los portadores mostraron un conocimiento limitado de los riesgos. Conclusión: el piercing oral genera complicaciones locales frecuentes y prevenibles que justifican la orientación profesional antes y después de su colocación.

title: Nicotina, productos de tabaco y salud bucal: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los efectos de la nicotina y de los productos de tabaco en la salud bucal. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas, metaanálisis, revisiones narrativas, un análisis de carga mundial de enfermedad y un estudio experimental. Resultados: el tabaquismo aumentó el riesgo de periodontitis, alteró la microcirculación y el microbioma bucal, y redujo la respuesta al tratamiento periodontal y a los implantes. La nicotina afectó la capacidad regenerativa de las células madre dentales. El tabaco se asoció con el cáncer bucal y con las tinciones dentales. Los cigarrillos electrónicos también alteraron los parámetros periodontales. Conclusión: el abandono del consumo mejora la salud periodontal, y el consultorio odontológico es un espacio adecuado para promoverlo.

title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

title: Prevención de errores quirúrgicos y diagnósticos en odontología: modelo integral de seguridad: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la prevención de errores quirúrgicos y diagnósticos en odontología y proponer los componentes de un modelo integral de seguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios de diseño variado. Resultados: los incidentes se relacionaron con el diagnóstico, el tratamiento y la comunicación; los litigios por mala praxis mostraron causas recurrentes; la tomografía computarizada de haz cónico y la inteligencia artificial mejoraron la precisión diagnóstica; la planificación del riesgo y la profilaxis antibiótica redujeron las complicaciones, y la comprensión del consentimiento informado por los pacientes fue limitada. Conclusión: la seguridad operatoria requiere integrar diagnóstico, planificación quirúrgica, comunicación y aprendizaje de los incidentes.

title: Efectos neurodegenerativos del consumo crónico de alcohol: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los efectos neurodegenerativos del consumo crónico de alcohol. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: cohortes, estudios de neuroimagen, revisiones sistemáticas y de alcance y revisiones de mecanismos. Resultados: los trastornos por consumo de alcohol triplicaron el riesgo de demencia, y el consumo superior a 14 unidades semanales se asoció con mayor riesgo. La neuroimagen mostró atrofia del hipocampo y menor volumen de sustancia gris y blanca con relación dosis-respuesta, sin efecto protector del consumo ligero. La neuroinflamación, el estrés oxidativo, la excitotoxicidad y la deficiencia de tiamina explican el daño. Conclusión: el consumo crónico e intenso es un factor de riesgo modificable de neurodegeneración y demencia.

title: Mala adherencia al tratamiento antihipertensivo e insuficiencia cardíaca: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre la mala adherencia al tratamiento antihipertensivo como factor que favorece el desarrollo de insuficiencia cardíaca. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: metaanálisis, ensayos clínicos, cohortes y guías de práctica clínica. Resultados: casi la mitad de los hipertensos no se adhiere al tratamiento, sobre todo por sus creencias sobre los fármacos. La baja adherencia se asoció con mayor mortalidad y hospitalización cardiovascular, y cada reducción de 10 mmHg de la presión sistólica disminuyó el riesgo de insuficiencia cardíaca. Conclusión: la mala adherencia mantiene la presión elevada y favorece la cardiopatía hipertensiva, por lo que su detección es una estrategia preventiva prioritaria.

title: 高校舞蹈教育中民族民间舞的传承与优化
abstractText: 民族民间舞是我国舞蹈艺术体系中的重要组成部分，承载着丰富的地域文化记忆与族群审美经验。高校舞蹈教育作为专业人才培养的主要渠道，在民族民间舞的传承中承担着不可替代的角色。然而，当前高校民族民间舞教育在课程设置、教学方法、师资结构以及评价机制等方面仍存在一些亟待解决的问题，影响了传承的深度与广度。本文围绕高校舞蹈教育中民族民间舞的传承现状展开分析，探讨其在文化认知、教学实践与资源整合方面的不足，进而从课程体系优化、教学方法改进、师资建设以及实践平台拓展等维度提出相应的优化路径。研究认为，民族民间舞的传承需要在保持文化内核的基础上，与当代教育理念和艺术实践形成有效衔接，从而实现从技艺传授到文化理解的深层转化。

title: AI赋能高校思政教学质量监测与反馈机制构建
abstractText: 高校思想政治教育的高质量发展，关键在于实现教学过程的精准化、教学评价的科学化与教学改进的常态化。AI技术凭借大数据挖掘、自然语言处理、智能研判等优势，为重构思政教学质量体系拓开了全新的思路。笔者围绕立德树人根本任务，阐述AI赋能思政教学质量的内在逻辑和价值，多角度构建智能化的思政教学质量监测与反馈机制，并针对性提出技术融合、师资赋能、制度完善、风险防控的实践策略，以期破解思政教学重结果轻过程、重评价轻改进的困境，推动高校思政教学从经验型育人向智慧型育人转变。

title: 天津非遗杨柳青年画的传承价值及其文创产品开发创新研究
abstractText: 杨柳青年画作为首批国家级非物质文化遗产，承载着中国北方深厚的民俗文化内涵。本文梳理杨柳青年画的历史脉络，从不同角度探究杨柳青年画的多维传承价值，通过查阅地方志与非遗档案等文献，深入杨柳青镇多家传统画庄进行调研观察，探究其作为文化旅游产品开发的现实困境，从文创形式多元化进行文创开发模式设计，并围绕视觉转译、材料拓展与场景重构提出文创开发策略，为杨柳青年画活态保护与文创产业化发展提供发展参考。

title: 新质生产力背景下民航通信技术专业建设与产教融合路径研究
abstractText: 新质生产力驱动下，尤其是低空经济时代的到来，民航通信技术正向空地一体、算力融合的智慧中枢加速演进，专业领域从运输航空向低空智联网、无人机通信等新场景延伸。这一变革对高职民航通信技术人才培养提出更高要求。本文提出以“教育—人才—产业—创新”四链融合为主线，构建课程体系重构、载体共建、校地协同、技术赋能四位一体的产教融合模式。针对技术迭代滞后等挑战，提出合理化建议，为民航通信技术专业在新质生产力背景下的转型升级提供路径参考。

title: 人工智能与数字化转型时代的佛教伦理
abstractText: 数字化转型加速了人工智能对社会生活的影响，传统伦理体系遭遇前所未有的挑战，而佛教拥有的智慧及严格的戒律要求，因果的法则，将成为人工智能的伦理治理提供有效的参考。本文先厘清人工智能发展现状及问题，然后系统讨论数字化场景中佛教修行及传播所面临的新问题，由此引出研究目标及核心问题：AI伦理可借鉴佛教“缘起性空”思想，促进人机良性互动，避免技术滥用。但佛教伦理在数字化转型中也面临信仰形式异化、传统遭解构、伦理落地难等问题。本文提出融合佛教智慧构建多元共治的AI伦理体系、推动佛教自身数字化良性转型、搭建人机共生的伦理体系等路径，让技术发展与人文伦理彼此协调、互为促进，最终实现“科技为体，佛法为魂”的良性互动。

title: 红色文化导向下职业院校舞蹈创编教学创新
abstractText: 红色文化是中国共产党领导人民在革命、建设与改革历程中积淀形成的先进文化，兵团文化为红色文化在边疆建设领域的重要分支，承载着几代兵团人扎根边疆、辛苦奋斗、无私奉献的精神，为职业教育开展德育教育提供了宝贵的素材。本文将从职业院校人才培养的核心目标出发，全面反思目前舞蹈创编教学中存在的共性问题，以红色文化为核心切入点，进一步完善教学体系、创新教学方法、拓展实践平台。通过红色文化与舞蹈创编教学的融合，促使学生肢体表达与艺术创新能力显著提升，同时在创编中领悟红色精神，实现全面发展，而这也为其他职业院校舞蹈类专业教学改革提供了有效的参考。

title: 中国古典园林造园艺术与景区规划建设的关系——以中国四大名园为案例探究
abstractText: 中国古典园林是东方造园艺术的杰出代表，“虚实结合”“因地制宜”等造园手法，充分体现出“天人合一”的生态智慧与人文精神。在当代进行景区规划建设的过程中，这些手法依然拥有重要的参考和启发价值，本文选取颐和园、拙政园、承德避暑山庄、留园四大名园作为研究案例，结合文献研究与案例分析，解析这类古典园林的核心造园手法，并探究这些手法如何在现代景区规划中完成转化与应用。研究结果表明，古典园林在意境营造、空间组织与功能整合等多个层面，都为现代景区给出了丰富的设计美学与文化表达依据，能够帮助景区在创新发展过程中传承文化脉络、塑造场所精神。

title: 《猫的摇篮》中的科技探讨与道德责任缺失
abstractText: 库尔特·冯内古特的《猫的摇篮》是一本研究意义、人性和知识内涵的文学作品，菲利克斯·霍尼克尔因为他的认知困境而被广泛关注——他有非常丰富的知识，但是不知道这些知识的价值何在。《猫的摇篮》中出现的是一个复杂的形势，那就是缺少足够的道德判断能力的人类智能主体，对于这个话题的研究不但可以打破传统的观念——即认为智力和智慧一定是有关系的，而且也促使我们重新思考人自身的价值判断标准。

title: 城市更新公共空间的展陈设计与可持续运营研究
abstractText: 在城市发展由增量向存量转变的过程中，如何通过公共空间的文化激活来解决城市更新问题成为一个重要的议题。而展陈设计正是给予空间叙事厚度和文化意义的重要方式，在众多的城市更新项目中，它更是起到画龙点睛的作用。但大量的公共空间却在开幕后的喧闹之后陷入了内容枯竭、脱离社区以及缺乏造血能力等问题之中——这暴露出展陈设计与空间运营之间的长久断裂。本文认为，要打破这种困局需要跳出“设计—建造—运营”的线性思考，建立一个“内容即运营”，“社区即主体”，“文化即引擎”的系统性协同关系：展陈设计应该从封闭的“白立方”转变为根植于在地语境的“强场域”叙事，并使空间变成不断生长的内容发生器；可持续的运营则是基于社区深入参与到的情感连接和社会资本形成，“展陈＋商业＋服务”的复合模式让文化的价值与经济的价值得到良性循环。只有把展陈设计作为一种可持续运营的一部分融入其中，城市更新中的公共空间才能够从一时的吸引到永久的活力，真正成为嵌入城市的日常的“文化基础设施”。

title: 稳定中的变化：中国儿童心理韧性结构的时代演变——基于元分析的证据
abstractText: 本研究结合横断历史元分析与传统元分析，对 2012—2025 年使用《中国青少年韧性量表 (RSCA)》的实证研究开展系统整合。共纳入 91 篇文献、546 个效应量，运用元回归、异质性分析、调节效应与亚组分析开展统计检验。结果显示：（1）近 13 年我国儿童心理韧性整体水平未出现显著时代变化，横断历史效应量偏小，目标专注、情绪控制、积极认知、家庭支持、人际协助五个维度同样保持相对稳定；（2）纳入研究存在极高异质性（I² = 98.77%）；（3）五个维度的研究均值均对总体心理韧性存在显著正向调节，维度标准差的调节效应整体偏弱；（4）发表年代无法直接预测心理韧性水平，但发表年代与五个维度均值的交互作用全部显著，说明随着时代发展，各保护维度与总体心理韧性的正向关联不断增强；（5）发表偏倚检验提示存在小样本效应，但未检出缺失研究，研究结果稳健。综上，近 13 年中国儿童心理韧性总体水平保持稳定，但内部保护性资源之间的关联模式发生时代性改变。
